pairs: And Judas heard of the fame of the Romans,
that they are powerful and strong,
et acquiescunt ad omnia quæ postulantur ab eis,
and that they willingly agree to all things that are asked of them;
and that, whoever was agreeable to them,
they established a friendship with them,
and so they are powerful and resourceful.
And they heard of their battles,
et virtutes bonas, quas fecerunt in Galatia,
and the successful works that they had accomplished in Galatia,
quia obtinuerunt eos, et duxerunt sub tributum:
how they had subdued them and brought them under tribute,
et quanta fecerunt in regione Hispaniæ,
and what great things they had accomplished in the region of Spain,
et quod in potestatem redegerunt metalla argenti et auri,
and that they had driven under their power the mines of silver
et possederunt omnem locum consilio suo,
and that they had obtained possession of the entire place by their counsel
locaque quæ longe erant valde ab eis,
and that they had overcome places that were very far from them,
qui supervenerant eis ab extremis terræ,
who came against them from the ends of the earth,
and struck them with a great scourging,
ceteri autem dant eis tributum omnibus annis.
while the rest pay tribute to them every year,
Et Philippum et Persen Ceteorum regem,
and that they had defeated in battle Philip,
et ceteros qui adversum eos arma tulerant,
and Perses the king of the Ceteans,
and the others who had taken up arms against them,
and had crushed them in warfare and subdued them,
and how Antiochus, the great king of Asia,
qui eis pugnam intulerat habens centum viginti elephantos,
who brought a fight against them, having one hundred and twenty elephants,
et currus, et exercitum magnum valde,
and swift chariots, and a very great army,
et quia ceperunt eum vivum, et statuerunt ei ut daret ipse, et qui regnarent post ipsum,
and how they had captured him alive and had decreed to him that both he and those who would reign after him would pay a great tribute,
tributum magnum, et daret obsides, et constitutum,
and that he should provide hostages bound to an agreement,
and that regions from the Indians,
with those whom they had taken from them,
et quia qui erant apud Helladam, voluerunt ire,
And those who were in Greece wanted to go out and defeat them,
et tollere eos: et innotuit sermo his,
but they became aware of this plan.
et miserunt ad eos ducem unum,
And so they sent one general to them,
et captivas duxerunt uxores eorum et filios,
and they led into captivity their wives,
and they despoiled them and took possession of their land,
and they destroyed their walls and drove them into servitude,
et in servitutem illos redegerunt usque in hunc diem:
which at any time had resisted them,
et qui in ipsis requiem habebant,
and with those who remained at peace with them,
they maintained friendship and conquered kingdoms:
and those that were far off.
quia quicumque audiebant nomen eorum, timebant eos:
For all those who heard of their name were afraid of them.
quibus vero vellent auxilio esse ut regnarent,
In fact, whomever they wanted to help become ruler,
Et in omnibus istis nemo portabat diadema,
none wore a diadem or was clothed in purple,
And also, they had made themselves a senate house,
et quotidie consulebant trecentos viginti consilium agentes semper de multitudine,
and they consulted daily with three hundred and twenty men, continually acting as a counsel for the multitude,
so that they would do the things that were right.
et committunt uni homini magistratum suum per singulos annos dominari universæ terræ suæ,
And they commit their government to one man each year,
to rule over their entire land,
and they all obey this one,
and there is no envy or jealousy among them.
Et elegit Judas Eupolemum filium Joannis filii Jacob,
And so Judas chose Eupolemus, the son of John, the son of Jacob,
and Jason, the son of Eleazar,
et misit eos Romam constituere cum illis amicitiam et societatem:
and he sent them to Rome to make an agreement of friendship and an alliance with them,
et ut auferrent ab eis jugum Græcorum,
and so that they would take away from them the yoke of the Grecians,
quia viderunt quod in servitutem premerent regnum Israël.
for they saw that they oppressed the kingdom of Israel with servitude.
Et abierunt Romam viam multam valde,
And they went to Rome, a very long journey,
and they entered the senate house,
and the people of the Jews,
miserunt nos ad vos statuere vobiscum societatem et pacem,
have sent us to you to establish with you an alliance and peace,
et conscribere nos socios et amicos vestros.
and so that we may be registered among your associates and friends.”
Et placuit sermo in conspectu eorum.
And the word was pleasing in their sight.
Et hoc rescriptum est quod rescripserunt in tabulis æreis,
And this is a copy of the writing,
which they rewrote on tablets of brass and sent to Jerusalem,
ut esset apud eos ibi memoriale pacis et societatis:
so that it would be with them in that place as a memorial of the peace and alliance:
“May all be well with the Romans and with the nation of the Jews,
in mari et in terra in æternum:
gladiusque et hostis procul sit ab eis.
and may sword and enemy be far away from them.
Quod si institerit bellum Romanis prius,
But if a war is instituted against the Romans first,
aut omnibus sociis eorum in omni dominatione eorum,
or against any of their allies in all their dominions,
the nation of the Jews will bring help to them,
just as the situation shall direct,
they need not provide with supplies of wheat,
just as it seems good to the Romans,
and they shall obey their orders,
et si genti Judæorum prius acciderit bellum,
if war will have fallen upon the nation of the Jews first,
the Romans shall help them willingly,
just as the situation permits them.
And those who give assistance will not be provided with wheat,
just as it seems good to the Romans.
et custodient mandata eorum absque dolo:
And they shall obey their orders without deceit.
secundum hæc verba constituerunt Romani populo Judæorum.
According to these words, the Romans have made an agreement with the people of the Jews.
Quod si post hæc verba hi
aut demere ad hæc aliquid voluerint,
one or another would want to add anything to,
they may do as they propose.
And whatever they add or take away,
quæ Demetrius rex fecit in eos,
concerning the evils that king Demetrius did to them,
Quare gravasti jugum tuum super amicos nostros,
‘Why have you made your yoke heavy upon our friends and allies,
If, therefore, they come again to us against you,
adversum te faciemus illis judicium, et pugnabimus tecum mari terraque.
we will render judgment for them, and we will make war against you by sea and by land.’”
